<objective>
The tracer slice for this phase: one real permission check wired from a database row through the
member seam and a new `access` gate to a real 403 on the wire, proven by a test that calls the
route directly.

Purpose: the phase risk sits in one question. Does a per-member, per-shed grant resolve cleanly at
the member seam and enforce at a sibling gate without touching the shed lookup? Proving it on one
route before four more handlers, a steward API and a page grow from it turns a dead end into a
one-commit discovery.

Output: `0004_roles_and_grants.sql`, `src/server/access/gate.ts`, a `Member` that carries role and
grants, the shed route call site, and a live-server test showing 403 without and non-403 with.
</objective>

<task type="checkpoint:decision" gate="blocking">
  <name>Task 1: Confirm the one-way schema shape before the migration is written</name>
  <decision>Commit to a two-value `members.role` column plus per-member grant rows, with no roles table and no role-grants table.</decision>
  <context>
This is the one decision in the phase that cannot be walked back by a code change. Once grant rows
exist, a later roles model needs a migration that invents groupings nobody chose today.

Two fixed roles keep the steward check a single comparison, and per-member rows keep the editable
grid small. The context file records that the lead steward weighed this and chose it.
  </context>
  <options>
    <option id="proceed">
      <name>Go ahead as drafted — two fixed roles, per-member grants, the migration promotes the oldest account to steward</name>
      <pros>Matches the locked decision exactly and leaves no moment with zero stewards.</pros>
      <cons>One-way: a future roles model needs a real migration, and onboarding a member means ticking their grid again.</cons>
    </option>
